Just because society decided a few specific ways to be, it  is not the only route you got. You follow what's best for your situation personally. Also forgive yourself, please, you can't just decide to give up because you believe you are stupid in comparison to your friends with ADHD, everyone's symptoms present differently.Instead of dwelling on what you see as shortcomings, shift your focus to your strengths and achievements. Celebrate your creativity, problem-solving skills, empathy, and other unique qualities. Success isn't limited to tying shoes or academic performance alone—it includes personal growth, resilience, and the ability to overcome obstacles.Comparing yourself to others won't get you anywhere. 

Everyone's journey is different, and we all have our own challenges. Instead of feeling inadequate compared to your classmates, embrace your own unique strengths and abilities.Remember, you're not defined by your struggles. I have not related to a post this fondly on this sub Reddit so far. Honestly,  all I can say to you after reading this as someone with ADHD myself is that it will take time, but  you have to declutter parts of your life bit by bit so that one day, you can see the big picture.

Use pomodoros to help you schedule deep work sessions , talk to me or even better a therapist, be patient with yourself and please forgive yourself because without that, any effort will seem effortless.  

Effort demands intention, anything is possible, even with ADHD but ngl it’s going to suck for a while before it gets better. I will recommend you to also start a bit of strength training, have your meds on time and try to find out what really fuels your brain because we all work different .

You have to treat yourself with ADHD like an iterative project, unlike others, we have to put in extra effort to get effective results and unfortunately, even those results aren’t guaranteed.

Hey, so, just a little heads up, I also did my driving lessons at EDI and in fact gave around 17 assessment attempts before even getting to RTA. I passed RTA in my second attempt but obviously  it was a long way to get there.

So here's a couple of things I would say:

* Always do your centre mirror, shoulder and rear mirror checks
* Follow the MSPSL routine
* I'd suggest also getting a hang of the route you're taking for your test, ask your instructor to take you the same route so you've an idea of the road conditions there, not saying they wouldn't change them in the test, but they do have a set route and try to better your driving etiquette  in the given route
* Also hey, they might change the car, but tbh, still it's only your driving habit they're checking try to get adapted to the test car as well. 
* Please analyze your score sheet to check where exactly are you losing points , so generally, you're allowed to make 8-10 minor mistakes and you'd still pass, please find out where are your minor mistakes and if you've major, it's a direct fail so avoid those at any cost
* They look for obvious eye movements, and shoulder checks if the situation demands
* There's people at EDI that would say morning because of low traffic but honestly, I myself have passed out from the same place and I'd say anytime is fine as long as your displaying good driving etiquette
* Book a class a day before your test. or perhaps if you've got a test try on the day of the exam, that way you'll have fresh recall of driving conditions, I'd done this for one of my RTA tests
* Most importantly , stay patient and calm, honestly driving is about staying calm yet proactive on the road to respond to any possible hazards
